name: Quarterly P&L Template
description:
# Quarterly P&L Template

Three-sheet workbook (Summary, Details, Charts) demonstrating a quarterly profit-and-loss layout: KPI header band, line-item table with Excel SUM formulas, and a side-by-side bar chart comparing Q1-Q4. Suitable as a structural reference for `apply_component` cells targeting `quarterly_report` archetypes.

## Layout
- **Summary** — 4-row KPI band (Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Net Income) with absolute values and YoY %
- **Details** — line items × quarters matrix with totals row
- **Charts** — embedded BarChart referencing Details!B2:E12

## Suggested use
Clone this layout when the agent needs a tidy P&L without inventing column structure from scratch.
applicability: Quarterly profit and loss reporting with KPI band, line-item detail, and side-by-side quarter comparison chart.

name: Inventory Dashboard
description:
# Inventory Dashboard

Single-sheet inventory tracker with conditional formatting on stock-level columns (red < 10, yellow < 25, green ≥ 25), VLOOKUP for product names, and a donut chart for category distribution. Demonstrates a tight 12-row × 6-col layout that fits on screen without scrolling.

## Cells of interest
- B2:G2 — KPI tiles (Total SKUs, Reorder Count, Out-of-Stock, Avg DOS)
- B4:G16 — main inventory table with conditional fill
- I4:O14 — donut chart by category
applicability: Inventory tracking dashboard with conditional formatting, VLOOKUP product names, and category donut chart.

name: Budget vs Actual Variance Report
description:
# Budget vs Actual Variance Report

Two-sheet variance report: (1) Budget — planned line items per cost center; (2) Actual — observed line items; with a third Variance sheet computed via cross-sheet formulas (=Actual!B2-Budget!B2) and conditional formatting that highlights overspend in red and underspend in green. Headers anchored at row 2 so they stay visible when the table grows.

## Formulas
- C2:C100 — `=Actual!B2-Budget!B2` (variance amount)
- D2:D100 — `=IFERROR(C2/Budget!B2, 0)` (variance %)
- E1 — `=SUM(C2:C100)` (total variance)

## Suggested use
Use this layout for any periodic plan-vs-observed comparison; the cross-sheet formulas generalise beyond budgets.
applicability: Plan-vs-actual variance reporting with cross-sheet formulas and conditional formatting on overspend/underspend.
